BiblicalUsage: gᵉʻârâh — a rebuke, reproof. That is the whole of it, and it is enough: 14 occurrences, and in 2 Samuel, Job, Psalms, and Proverbs the meaning never wavers. I keep coming back to the simple reading because the simple reading is the true one.
TheologicalSignificance: What gᵉʻârâh tells me is that a rebuke spoken in love is a mercy, not an insult. I hold that the simple reading is the true one, and I will not trade it for a clever one.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
